description: SE student at SSUET (Karachi) with experience in Python, FastAPI, LangChain, RAG and ML. I'm building The Earth Information Jukebox: a web app that turns NASA temperature and rainfall data into music, so people can hear our planet change. I'll handle data, backend and sonification. Need a JavaScript frontend dev, a music/Tone.js enthusiast, and a UI/UX or video editor. Beginners welcome!
summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is an accessible web application that transforms NASA Earth observation videos and satellite maps into sound (data sonification). Built for NASA Space Apps Challenge #14, the project addresses the sensory barrier of visual-only planetary data, enabling blind and low-vision individuals—as well as students and researchers—to explore dynamic Earth systems through auditory perception.

The platform operates in two modes: Video Mode converts satellite video frames (Air Quality, Weather, CO₂, and Space) into natural acoustic soundscapes with spatial stereo panning; Picture Mode maps satellite layers (Sea Surface Temperature, Rain, Snow, Aerosols, and Vegetation) to calibrated musical tones based on official NASA data legends. 

Running 100% client-side in the browser with zero backend or tracking, it provides total user privacy, offline resilience, live screen-reader captions, and synchronized video/audio downloads, democratizing planetary science for everyone regardless of visual acuity.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Earth Information Jukebox is an accessible web platform that converts NASA Earth observation imagery and videos into sound—a process known as data sonification. It allows users to "listen" to planetary phenomena across space and time.

https://youtu.be/PH4HPXgdGh8?si=tTDD6ra1onvFLTcd

The application operates in two core modes:

A. Video Sonification Mode

- Supported Datasets: Air Quality (PM2.5 particulate matter), Weather (Near-surface wind dynamics), Carbon Dioxide (CO2 atmospheric plumes), and Space (Star clusters & deep-space imagery).

- Frame Analysis: Video streams are sampled at 4 frames per second and segmented into 32 vertical geographic strips.

- Feature Extraction: Pixel colors and intensities are computed into normalized density metrics (0 to 1):

• Air Quality: Smoke and dust density modulate low-frequency rumble and particulate crackle.

• Weather: Color shifts from blue (mild) to red (extreme) govern wind turbulence and filter resonance.

• CO2 Plumes: Golden haze and dense gas patches drive ambient drone textures, designed to be immune to camera zoom artifacts.

• Space Radar: Employs a custom temporal median algorithm across frames to isolate static stars from moving lines, sweeping a 360° radar beam where radial distance sets pitch and brightness sets volume.

- Spatialized Scanning: An indicator line sweeps left-to-right across the video with dynamic stereo panning, directing sound to the corresponding ear.

B. Satellite Map / Picture Mode

- Supported Layers: Sea Surface Temperature (GHRSST), Precipitation Rate (IMERG Rain & Snow), Aerosol Optical Depth (VIIRS), Vegetation Index (NDVI), plus a brightness fallback for any uploaded photo.

- Perceptual Color Classification: Slices maps into a 96-zone grid (32 strips × 3 latitude regions: North, Middle, South). Pixels are converted into the CIELAB color space and evaluated against official NASA legend ramps using ΔE76 Euclidean distance to determine the true scientific data band.

- Multi-Timbral Acoustic Engine: Assigns specific instruments to match the physical character of each dataset:

• Temperature: Soft piano tones ascending from cold to warm.

• Precipitation: Organic water droplets for rain; music-box bells for snow.

• Aerosols: Warm, resonant atmospheric pads.

• Vegetation: Earthy, percussive soft marimba.

• Custom Images: Kalimba tuned to luminance.

- Scan Trajectories: Users can traverse the data via an intuitive Zig-Zag path (North → South, then South → North across adjacent strips) or a Straight linear path.

C. Built-in Export Pipeline

Utilizes HTML5 Canvas and the Web Audio API to render synchronized video (MP4/WebM) with audio and moving scanlines, alongside instant 16-bit stereo WAV audio downloads.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Sensory Inclusion for the Visually Impaired: Blind and low-vision individuals can independently explore, comprehend, and analyze complex geospatial data without needing sight.

- Dual-Modality Learning: Sighted researchers, educators, and students benefit from multisensory reinforcement—hearing a sudden spike in aerosol density or ocean temperature while watching the map sharpens pattern recognition and anomaly detection.

- 100% Client-Side Privacy & Zero Cost: All signal processing, video decoding, and audio synthesis happen directly in the user’s browser. No data ever leaves the local machine, eliminating cloud compute bills and protecting user-uploaded files.

- Instant Usability: Zero installation, zero account registration, and zero dependencies—works instantly on desktop, tablet, or mobile.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

- Universal Access to Earth Science: Demystifies NASA Earth Science data by eliminating visual-only barriers. Planetary observation becomes accessible to everyone, regardless of visual acuity.

- Classroom & STEM Engagement: Serves as a hands-on pedagogical tool for K-12 and university curricula to teach climate change, atmospheric circulation, and remote sensing through sound.

- Citizen Science Empowerment: Equips amateur astronomers and environmental enthusiasts to upload their own regional captures to audit air quality or weather events auditorily.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Languages & Web Standards:

• Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules): Lightweight, modular, zero-dependency runtime code.

• HTML5 Canvas & Semantic markup: High-framerate overlay rendering and screen-reader accessibility.

• Modern CSS3: Custom design tokens, glassmorphism, responsive Grid/Flexbox layouts.

- Audio & Digital Signal Processing (DSP):

• Web Audio API: AudioContext, GainNodes, StereoPannerNodes, and MediaStreamDestination.

• Custom Pure-JS DSP Engine: RBJ biquad filters (lowpass/bandpass), one-pole smoothers, seeded pseudo-random noise (mulberry32 + Box-Muller Gaussian transform), ADSR envelope shaping, and custom Float32-to-WAV encoders.

• Web Workers: Executes heavy mathematical synthesis off the main UI thread to prevent interface stutter.

- Color Science:

• RGB to CIELAB space conversion and ΔE76 minimum-distance matching algorithms against official NASA colormap XML specifications.

- Build, Test & Deployment Stack:

• Vite & Node.js: Ultra-fast build and bundling toolchain.

• Vitest: Unit testing for DSP frequency bounds, spectral balance, and color classification accuracy.

• Playwright: End-to-end automated testing for UI rendering, scanline movement, and audio sync.

• @axe-core/playwright & Lighthouse: Automated WCAG 2.1 accessibility and performance audits.

• ffmpeg-static / ffprobe: Video transcoding, frame extraction validation, and temporal median computation.

• Vercel: Global edge hosting and deployment.

5. How is your project creative?

- Calibrated Acoustic Metaphors, Not Random Music: Instead of generating arbitrary songs or harsh synthetic beeps, the system employs psychoacoustically grounded sounds that mirror real physical phenomena—wind friction, crackling dust, raindrops, and crystalline bells.

- Binaural Spatial Geography: Longitude maps directly to stereo panning (left to right ear), giving the listener a distinct three-dimensional mental map of global data coordinates.

- Temporal Median Video Deconstruction: In Space mode, the system analyzes 40 distributed frames to mathematically subtract dynamic NASA HUD lines, producing a pristine star field for custom polar radar sonification.

- "Night + Glass" Aesthetic: Fuses Swiss typographic clarity with a dark, high-contrast glassmorphic cockpit that satisfies both aesthetic elegance and rigorous accessibility standards.

6. What factors did your team consider?

- Accessibility First (WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA Compliance):

• Polite Screen-Reader Speech: Live audio captions use aria-live="polite" and are rate-limited to at most one update per second to prevent overwhelming speech synthesizers.

• Multi-Modal Redundancy: Information is never communicated by color alone. Every data point is presented through sound, visual position, color swatch, human-readable color label, numerical value, and note pitch in a semantic <table>.

• Full Keyboard Navigation: Dedicated hotkeys (Space for play/pause, M for mute, G for generate, ← / → for single-step nudges) with prominent focus rings and zero keyboard traps.

• System Preferences: Full support for prefers-reduced-motion (disabling animated backdrops) and prefers-reduced-transparency / forced-colors.

- Scientific Integrity:

• A strict "Never Invent Data" policy—all color classification ranges are referenced directly against official NASA colormaps (GMAO, SVS, GHRSST, and VIIRS).

- Hardware & Bandwidth Equity:

• Designed to run efficiently on low-spec hardware, budget Chromebooks, and mobile browsers without requiring a dedicated GPU or high-speed internet. All sample media files are strictly compressed under tight megabyte budgets.
